title: Models-as-a-Service (MaaS) core: access model and token mechanism

steps.caption: The workshop model is deployed and published to MaaS: the deployment row shows Ready, and the details confirm Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) availability on a CPU-only cluster.
Models published to MaaS appear on the AI asset endpoints page: each row shows the model ID, the use case, the operational status, and an Endpoints View button.
The Endpoints dialog shows the Model as a Service badge, the external API endpoint URL for the MaaS gateway, and the subscription that governs this model.
Generate API key mints a 1-hour temporary key: it carries the sk-oai- prefix, is displayed only once (masked here), and never appears in your API keys list.
For a persistent key, open Gen AI studio > API keys. The table lists every key with its status, subscription, owner, and expiration.
Click Create API key: a persistent key needs a name, the subscription that scopes it, and an expiration between 1 and 365 days.

details.label: Subscription
details.value: scopes the key to one subscription

steps.caption: Name the key, select the p2w12-maas-demo subscription - the dialog lists the models it includes with their token limits - and set expiration to 90 days.
The plaintext key is displayed only during creation and cannot be retrieved later: copy it and store it securely before closing the dialog.

details.label: Warning
details.value: Save your API key - shown only once

steps.caption: The key appears in the list with Status Active, bound to your subscription. A gateway call with it returns an OpenAI-compatible response whose usage object is the token mechanism made visible.
